Fix a field $k$. In the ordinary categorical case, a **finite semisimple fusion category over $k$** is a finite semisimple tensor category in the sense of the earlier fusion-and-multifusion definition. Concretely, it is a locally small category (each Hom collection is a set) whose Hom spaces are $k$-vector spaces and whose composition maps are $k$-bilinear. A monomorphism $u:Y\to X$ is a morphism for which precomposition $\operatorname{Hom}(Z,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Z,X)$ is injective for every object $Z$; a subobject of $X$ is an isomorphism class of monomorphisms into $X$. An epimorphism is defined by the dual cancellation condition. The category is abelian: it has finite biproducts, kernels, and cokernels, every monomorphism is a kernel, and every epimorphism is a cokernel. Each Hom space is finite-dimensional, and every object has finite length, meaning a finite composition series with simple quotients. A simple object is nonzero with only the zero subobject and itself as subobjects; every object is a finite direct sum of simple objects, and only finitely many simple isomorphism classes occur. It has a $k$-bilinear tensor bifunctor, a tensor unit $\mathbf 1$ with $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf 1)\cong k$, and a natural associator $\alpha_{X,Y,Z}:(X\otimes Y)\otimes Z\to X\otimes(Y\otimes Z)$ and left and right unitors satisfying the pentagon and triangle axioms.

For an object $X$, a left dual $X^L$ consists of morphisms $\operatorname{ev}_L:X^L\otimes X\to\mathbf 1$ and $\operatorname{coev}_L:\mathbf 1\to X\otimes X^L$ for which
$$(\operatorname{id}_X\otimes\operatorname{ev}_L)\circ\alpha_{X,X^L,X}\circ(\operatorname{coev}_L\otimes\operatorname{id}_X)=\operatorname{id}_X, \qquad (\operatorname{ev}_L\otimes\operatorname{id}_{X^L})\circ\alpha^{-1}_{X^L,X,X^L}\circ(\operatorname{id}_{X^L}\otimes\operatorname{coev}_L)=\operatorname{id}_{X^L}.$$
A right dual $X^R$ consists of $\operatorname{ev}_R:X\otimes X^R\to\mathbf 1$ and $\operatorname{coev}_R:\mathbf 1\to X^R\otimes X$ for which
$$(\operatorname{ev}_R\otimes\operatorname{id}_X)\circ\alpha^{-1}_{X,X^R,X}\circ(\operatorname{id}_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_R)=\operatorname{id}_X, \qquad (\operatorname{id}_{X^R}\otimes\operatorname{ev}_R)\circ\alpha_{X^R,X,X^R}\circ(\operatorname{coev}_R\otimes\operatorname{id}_{X^R})=\operatorname{id}_{X^R}.$$
The unitors are suppressed in these four composites. Rigidity means that each object has both kinds of dual.

For the ordinary fusion-category clauses below, write $\mathcal C$ for this category.

Choose representatives $i\in I$ of the finitely many simple-object isomorphism classes, with $0\in I$ representing $\mathbf 1$. For each $i,j,\ell\in I$, the **fusion multiplicity** $N_{ij}^{\ell}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ is the number of copies of $\ell$ in a semisimple decomposition of $i\otimes j$, so $i\otimes j\cong\bigoplus_{\ell\in I}N_{ij}^{\ell}\ell$. The associated fusion space is $V_{ij}^{\ell}:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(i\otimes j,\ell)$. For $D_\ell:=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\ell)$, simplicity makes $D_\ell$ a finite-dimensional division $k$-algebra and $V_{ij}^{\ell}$ a left $D_\ell$-module by postcomposition; its rank as a left $D_\ell$-module is $N_{ij}^{\ell}$. When $D_\ell=k$ (in particular for absolutely simple objects), $\dim_k V_{ij}^{\ell}=N_{ij}^{\ell}$.

For simple $i,j,k,\ell$, the associator induces an isomorphism between the two fusion-channel spaces
$$\bigoplus_{m\in I} V_{mk}^{\ell}\otimes_{D_m}V_{ij}^{m} \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ } \bigoplus_{n\in I} V_{in}^{\ell}\otimes_{D_n}V_{jk}^{n}.$$
Here $V_{mk}^{\ell}$ is a right $D_m$-module by $g\cdot d=g\circ(d\otimes\operatorname{id}_k)$, $V_{ij}^{m}$ is a left $D_m$-module by $d\cdot f=d\circ f$, $V_{in}^{\ell}$ is a right $D_n$-module by $f\cdot d=f\circ(\operatorname{id}_i\otimes d)$, and $V_{jk}^{n}$ is a left $D_n$-module by postcomposition. The isomorphism is defined by the semisimple decomposition identifications with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}((i\otimes j)\otimes k,\ell)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(i\otimes(j\otimes k),\ell)$, and the middle map sends $h$ to $h\circ\alpha^{-1}_{i,j,k}$. Thus its domain and codomain are the stated fusion-channel spaces, not unspecified multiplicity symbols. In chosen decompositions and bases these are the associator matrices; their coherence is the pentagon. The fusion datum includes the actual associator, unitors, and both duality structures, not just the integers $N_{ij}^{\ell}$; the unitors satisfy the triangle and the dual maps satisfy the four displayed snake identities.

A **tensor-invertible object** $D$ is an object for which some object $E$ satisfies $D\otimes E\cong\mathbf 1$ and $E\otimes D\cong\mathbf 1$. An object with no such two-sided inverse is **non-invertible**. Simplicity and tensor-invertibility are separate properties: an object can be simple and non-invertible, or a direct sum of invertible simple objects and non-invertible as a whole.

For the **finite semisimple fusion 2-category** convention, assume that $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero. A strict $k$-linear 2-category $\mathcal C$ has objects $A,B,\ldots$, a $k$-linear category $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(A,B)$ for each ordered pair, 1-morphisms as its objects, and 2-morphisms as its morphisms; horizontal composition is $k$-bilinear and strictly associative and unital, and satisfies interchange. A $k$-linear category is one whose morphism spaces are $k$-vector spaces and whose composition is $k$-bilinear. A finite semisimple $k$-linear category is an abelian $k$-linear category with finite-dimensional Hom spaces, finitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects, and every object a finite direct sum of simple objects; in each such category a simple object is nonzero with no nonzero proper subobject, using the ordinary categorical subobject convention above.

A functor between categories is **fully faithful** when it induces a bijection on morphism sets for each pair of objects. For 1-morphisms $p:A\to B$ and $q:B\to A$, an adjunction $p\dashv q$ consists of 2-morphisms (unit) $\eta:\operatorname{id}_A\Rightarrow q\circ p$ and (counit) $\epsilon:p\circ q\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_B$ satisfying $(\epsilon\star p)\cdot(p\star\eta)=\operatorname{id}_p$ and $(q\star\epsilon)\cdot(\eta\star q)=\operatorname{id}_q$, where $\star$ denotes whiskering by 1-morphisms and $\cdot$ denotes vertical composition of 2-morphisms. A 1-morphism $f:A\to B$ is **adjointable** when there are 1-morphisms $l,r:B\to A$ with $l\dashv f\dashv r$, with each adjunction carrying the unit, counit, and triangle identities just specified.

A zero object $0$ is an object for which each Hom category $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,0)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(0,X)$ is equivalent to the zero category, the category with one object and one morphism. A zero 1-morphism is a zero object in its Hom category. A 1-morphism $f:A\to B$ is **fully faithful** when for every object $X$, postcomposition with $f$ gives a fully faithful functor $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,A)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,B)$. A **subobject** of $B$ is an equivalence class of fully faithful 1-morphisms $f:A\to B$, where $f:A\to B$ and $g:A'\to B$ represent the same class exactly when there is an equivalence $u:A\to A'$ and an invertible 2-morphism $g\circ u\Rightarrow f$. A zero subobject is represented by a fully faithful 1-morphism whose domain is equivalent to a zero object. A 1-morphism $f:A\to B$ is an equivalence if there is a 1-morphism $g:B\to A$ and invertible 2-morphisms $g\circ f\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$ and $f\circ g\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_B$; two objects are equivalent when there is such an equivalence between them. A nonzero object (one not equivalent to a zero object) is **simple** when all its subobjects are represented by either a zero-domain 1-morphism or an equivalence.

An additive category is a category with a zero object and finite biproducts. A 2-category is **additive** when each Hom category is additive in this sense, it has a zero object, and finite direct sums of objects exist. For $A_1,A_2$, a direct sum $A_1\oplus A_2$ has inclusions $\iota_i:A_i\to A_1\oplus A_2$ and projections $\rho_i:A_1\oplus A_2\to A_i$ with $\rho_i\iota_i\cong\operatorname{id}_{A_i}$, $\rho_i\iota_j$ a zero 1-morphism for $i\ne j$, and $\operatorname{id}_{A_1\oplus A_2}\cong\iota_1\rho_1\oplus\iota_2\rho_2$ in its endomorphism category.

A **monad** on $B$ is a 1-morphism $E:B\to B$ with unit $\eta:\operatorname{id}_B\Rightarrow E$ and multiplication $m:E\circ E\Rightarrow E$ satisfying
$$
m\cdot(\eta\star E)=\operatorname{id}_E=m\cdot(E\star\eta),\qquad m\cdot(m\star E)=m\cdot(E\star m).
$$
It is **separable** when there is an $E$-bimodule 2-morphism $c:E\Rightarrow E\circ E$ such that
$$
c\cdot m=(m\star E)\cdot(E\star c)=(E\star m)\cdot(c\star E),\qquad m\cdot c=\operatorname{id}_E.
$$
The first equation says that $c$ respects the left and right $E$-actions, and the second says that it is a section of multiplication. An isomorphism of monads $\tau:E\Rightarrow F$ is an invertible 2-morphism respecting the units and multiplications: $\tau\cdot\eta_E=\eta_F$ and $\tau\cdot m_E=m_F\cdot(F\star\tau)\cdot(\tau\star E)$.

A **separable splitting** of $E:B\to B$ consists of an object $A$, an adjunction $\rho\dashv\iota$ with $\rho:B\to A$, $\iota:A\to B$, unit $\theta:\operatorname{id}_B\Rightarrow\iota\circ\rho$, and counit $\epsilon:\rho\circ\iota\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$, a 2-morphism section $s:\operatorname{id}_A\Rightarrow\rho\circ\iota$ with $\epsilon\cdot s=\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{id}_A}$, and an isomorphism of monads $E\cong\iota\circ\rho$, where $\iota\circ\rho$ has unit $\theta$ and multiplication $\iota\star\epsilon\star\rho$. A 2-category is **finite semisimple** when its Hom categories are finite semisimple, every 1-morphism is adjointable, it is additive, every separable monad has a separable splitting, and it has finitely many equivalence classes of simple objects.

Use the following semistrict monoidal 2-category convention (a Gray monoid). It adds a unit object $I$, strict $k$-linear 2-functors $L_A=A\otimes-$ and $R_A=-\otimes A$ for every object $A$, and for every pair of 1-morphisms $f:A\to A'$ and $g:B\to B'$ an invertible interchanger
$$\phi_{f,g}:(f\otimes B')\circ(A\otimes g)\Rightarrow(A'\otimes g)\circ(f\otimes B).$$
Write $A\otimes B=L_A(B)=R_B(A)$. The tensor is strictly unital and associative: $L_I=R_I=\operatorname{id}$, $L_A L_B=L_{A\otimes B}$, $R_B R_A=R_{A\otimes B}$, and $L_A R_B=R_B L_A$. The interchanger is the identity when either 1-morphism is an identity, is natural in both 2-morphisms, is compatible with composition in each 1-morphism variable, and is compatible with tensoring by an object in either variable. These are coherence axioms on the data, not consequences of a fusion table.

An object $A^R$ is a right dual of $A$ when there are evaluation and coevaluation 1-morphisms $e_R:A\otimes A^R\to I$ and $i_R:I\to A^R\otimes A$ and invertible 2-morphisms exhibiting $(e_R\otimes A)\circ(A\otimes i_R)\cong\operatorname{id}_A$ and $(A^R\otimes e_R)\circ(i_R\otimes A^R)\cong\operatorname{id}_{A^R}$. A left dual $A^L$ has evaluation $e_L:A^L\otimes A\to I$ and coevaluation $i_L:I\to A\otimes A^L$, with invertible 2-morphisms exhibiting $(A\otimes e_L)\circ(i_L\otimes A)\cong\operatorname{id}_A$ and $(e_L\otimes A^L)\circ(A^L\otimes i_L)\cong\operatorname{id}_{A^L}$. A **fusion 2-category** in this convention is a finite semisimple monoidal 2-category in which every object has left and right duals and the monoidal unit is simple.

Neither finite semisimplicity nor either categorical definition asserts unitarity: a dagger structure, positivity, and any unitary coherence are additional hypotheses and data. These are abstract mathematical structures. They do not construct defect operators or junctions in a quantum field theory, specify spacetime support, or prove topological invariance; a physical realization requires a separately specified model and its own construction and proof.

The ordinary associator pentagon below displays the two composites that the axiom requires to agree. This diagram records that axiom; no proof or example verification relies on the drawing.

```tikzcd
& (((W\otimes X)\otimes Y)\otimes Z) \arrow[rr,"\alpha_{W\otimes X,Y,Z}"] \arrow[dl,"\alpha_{W,X,Y}\otimes 1_Z"'] & & (W\otimes X)\otimes(Y\otimes Z) \arrow[dr,"\alpha_{W,X,Y\otimes Z}"] & \\
(W\otimes(X\otimes Y))\otimes Z \arrow[rr,"\alpha_{W,X\otimes Y,Z}"'] & & W\otimes((X\otimes Y)\otimes Z) \arrow[ur,"1_W\otimes\alpha_{X,Y,Z}"'] & & W\otimes(X\otimes(Y\otimes Z))
```

Let the scalar field be $\mathbb C$ and let the simple labels be $\mathbf 1$, $\psi$, and $\sigma$. Define a $\mathbb C$-linear semisimple category candidate whose objects are finite direct sums of these labels, whose simple-label Hom space is $\mathbb C$ when the labels agree and $0$ otherwise, and whose Hom spaces between direct sums are the corresponding finite matrices. Give the simple-label fusion product by

$$
\mathbf 1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf 1=a,\qquad \psi\otimes\psi=\mathbf 1,\qquad \psi\otimes\sigma=\sigma\otimes\psi=\sigma,\qquad \sigma\otimes\sigma=\mathbf 1\oplus\psi.
$$

Extend the product bilinearly to direct sums and on morphisms by the induced tensor product of scalar maps. The unit is $\mathbf 1$ and the unitors are strict. Fusion spaces are $V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$; each is one-dimensional when the displayed fusion rule allows $c$ and is zero otherwise. In every allowed one-dimensional fusion space choose its displayed basis vector. On three simple labels, define the associator in these bases by the matrix $[F^{abc}_d]_{xy}$, where $x$ is the intermediate label in $(a\otimes b)\otimes c\to d$ and $y$ is the intermediate label in $a\otimes(b\otimes c)\to d$. Set

$$
\left[F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma}\right]_{xy}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}_{xy},\qquad x,y\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi\},
$$

$$
\left[F^{\psi\sigma\psi}_{\sigma}\right]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,\qquad \left[F^{\sigma\psi\sigma}_{\psi}\right]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1.
$$

Every other coefficient is $1$ when all four fusion vertices are allowed and $0$ when any required fusion vertex is forbidden. Extend each associator linearly over direct sums. The candidate dual of each simple label is itself. For $\mathbf 1$ and $\psi$, take evaluation and coevaluation to be the unit-channel basis maps with coefficient $1$. For $\sigma$, take evaluation $\sigma\otimes\sigma\to\mathbf 1$ and coevaluation $\mathbf 1\to\sigma\otimes\sigma$ to have coefficient $2^{1/4}$ in the $\mathbf 1$ channel and zero in the $\psi$ channel. This item specifies the data; the separate coherence result checks that they satisfy the fusion-category axioms. No braiding or physical realization is included in this definition.

A **monoidal category** is a category $\mathcal C$ equipped with:

- a bifunctor $\otimes:\mathcal C\times\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$
  ([[def-product-category]], [[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]]);
- an object $\mathbf 1$ of $\mathcal C$;
- natural isomorphisms ([[def-natural-isomorphism]])
  $$\alpha_{X,Y,Z}:((X\otimes Y)\otimes Z)\longrightarrow X\otimes(Y\otimes Z),$$
  $$\lambda_X:(\mathbf 1\otimes X)\longrightarrow X,\qquad \rho_X:(X\otimes\mathbf 1)\longrightarrow X,$$

such that the following two equations hold for all objects
$W,X,Y,Z\in\mathcal C$.

The **pentagon axiom** is

$$\alpha_{W,X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{W\otimes X,Y,Z}=(1_W\otimes\alpha_{X,Y,Z})\circ\alpha_{W,X\otimes Y,Z}\circ(\alpha_{W,X,Y}\otimes1_Z).$$

The **triangle axiom** is

$$(1_X\otimes\lambda_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,\mathbf 1,Y}=\rho_X\otimes1_Y.$$

This page imposes no further axiom. In particular, the equality
$\lambda_{\mathbf 1}=\rho_{\mathbf 1}$ is not built into the definition; it is
derived later on this page.

derivations.claim: For triples with no unit label, the two bracketings have the same direct-sum decomposition: $\psi\psi\psi$ gives $\psi$; $\psi\psi\sigma$, $\psi\sigma\psi$, and $\sigma\psi\psi$ give $\sigma$; $\psi\sigma\sigma$, $\sigma\psi\sigma$, and $\sigma\sigma\psi$ give $\mathbf 1\oplus\psi$; and $\sigma\sigma\sigma$ gives $2\sigma$. Triples containing $\mathbf 1$ reduce by the explicitly specified canonical unitors. Thus the fusion products define the same channel bases on both sides of each associator. Each component category of finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and linear maps has kernels and cokernels (the underlying finite-dimensional vector-space kernels and quotients with induced Hilbert structures), and each subspace has an orthogonal complement; hence the triple category is abelian and every short exact sequence splits. It has exactly three simple isomorphism classes, all Hom spaces are finite-dimensional, every object is a finite direct sum of simples, and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf 1)=\mathbb C$, so it is finite semisimple with simple unit.

The dagger is conjugate-linear, involutive, and contravariant for composition because it is the Hilbert adjoint on every multiplicity block; the trace pairing also gives $\langle g\circ f,h\rangle=\langle f,g^\dagger\circ h\rangle$ for composable maps by direct substitution in each block. All weights $d_a$ are positive, so the displayed Hom inner product is positive definite. The weights are multiplicative across the fusion rules: $d_{\mathbf 1}d_a=d_a$, $d_\psi^2=d_{\mathbf 1}$, $d_\psi d_\sigma=d_\sigma$, and $d_\sigma^2=d_{\mathbf 1}+d_\psi$. Thus, for morphisms $f,f':X\to X'$ and $g,g':Y\to Y'$, expanding the tensor-product blocks gives $\langle f\otimes g,f'\otimes g'\rangle=\sum_{a,b,c}d_cN_{ab}^c\operatorname{Tr}(f_a^\dagger f'_a)\operatorname{Tr}(g_b^\dagger g'_b)=\langle f,f'\rangle\langle g,g'\rangle$, with the identity extending by sesquilinearity to finite sums. The tensor product is dagger-compatible since each block is a direct sum of Kronecker products of the component maps. The associator acts by the stated $F$ matrices on fusion-channel factors and by identity maps on multiplicity factors, whereas morphisms act on multiplicity factors; hence every naturality square commutes. Its Hadamard block divided by $\sqrt2$ is unitary, as are the one-channel blocks $1$ and $-1$, so the associator is unitary; the canonical unitors are unitary because their fusion-basis factors have norm one. On the dual multiplicity spaces, the left evaluation is the adjoint of the right coevaluation and the right evaluation is the adjoint of the left coevaluation: each adjoint is the canonical dual-basis pairing map in the same ordered tensor factors, with the same positive coefficient $\lambda_a$.

In the pentagon equation, write $F^{abc}_d[x,y]=0$ whenever either intermediate fusion channel is forbidden. For each choice of simple labels $a,b,c,d,e,f,g,k,\ell\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi,\sigma\}$, the two paths are $F^{fcd}_e[g,\ell]F^{ab\ell}_e[f,k]=\sum_{h\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi,\sigma\}}F^{abc}_g[f,h]F^{ahd}_e[g,k]F^{bcd}_k[h,\ell]$. The exact checker `research/advanced-qft-supersymmetry-build-2026-10-23-batch-39-ising-pentagon-check.py` substitutes the specified $F$-rules using rational arithmetic in $\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)$ over all $3^9=19{,}683$ outer label assignments. It finds 132 assignments with a nonzero side, verifies equality in all 132, and finds the remaining 19,551 assignments are $0=0$. The checker exits successfully only at those exact totals. Thus the pentagon holds for simple labels; multilinearity extends it to finite direct sums.

Every associator coefficient involving $\mathbf 1$ is $1$. On an elementary tensor $(v\otimes z\otimes u_{a\mathbf 1}^a)\otimes w\otimes u_{ab}^c$ in $(X\otimes\mathbf 1)\otimes Y$, the route through the associator and the left unitor sends it to $v\otimes zw\otimes u_{ab}^c$, while the route through the right unitor sends it to $zv\otimes w\otimes u_{ab}^c$. These are equal by the balancing relation of the complex tensor product. Such tensors span, proving the triangle for all objects. For $\psi$, each of the two snake composites has scalar $1\cdot1=1$. For $\sigma$, each composite uses the unit-channel associator coefficient $[F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma}]_{\mathbf 1,\mathbf 1}=1/\sqrt2$ and the two duality coefficients $\lambda_\sigma=2^{1/4}$, giving $\lambda_\sigma^2/\sqrt2=1$; the $\psi$ channel contributes zero because its evaluation coefficient is zero. For $X=(H_a)_a$, the dual object and both coevaluations are the stated direct sums of dual-basis tensors, while evaluation pairs only equal simple labels. Consequently every off-diagonal simple-label block of either snake composite is zero, and on each multiplicity space $H_a$ the dual-basis contraction is the identity multiplied by the corresponding simple-label snake scalar just computed. Both snake identities therefore hold for arbitrary finite direct sums, not only for simple labels.

The candidate has finite-dimensional Hom spaces, exactly three simple isomorphism classes, and every object a finite direct sum of simples; its unit is simple. Its tensor product is bilinear and its natural associator and canonical unitors satisfy the pentagon and triangle, while every object has the left and right duals and snake identities checked above. By [F1] it is a finite semisimple fusion category. Step 1.2 additionally supplies the positive dagger structure, proves tensor compatibility, and verifies unitary associators and adjoint duality maps, so the category is unitary in the explicit sense defined in the Statement. This is a purely mathematical result and makes no QFT-realization claim.

Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and a smooth $d$-manifold $M$, possibly with boundary. Fix the metric and signature, orientation and any time orientation, the geometric background bundles or lifts required by the model, and the boundary conditions. A **selected model** $\mathcal T$ on $M$ consists of a specified configuration space $\mathcal C_{\mathcal T}(M)$ of fields, including each field bundle, regularity class, and admissible boundary behavior; a collection of local observables with their types and supports; a set $\mathcal B_{\mathcal T}$ of admissible combined background and boundary data; and a set $\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}$ of admissible complete insertion inputs. An element of $\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}$ records data $b\in\mathcal B_{\mathcal T}$ and a finite ordered list whose entries are local observable insertions or other model-declared insertion data, together with the model's admissibility conditions on supports and labels. The model supplies a value space $\mathcal V_{\mathcal T}$ with a specified topology and a correlator functional $C_{\mathcal T}:\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}\to\mathcal V_{\mathcal T}$ with an explicit normalization convention, which may be normalized or unnormalized; the notation $C_{\mathcal T}(b;D;X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ denotes its value on the complete input with combined background and boundary data $b$, defect data $D$, and other insertion data $X_i$. The model also fixes its unit system, action and charge normalizations, and any regulator, measure, or renormalization prescription used to define $C_{\mathcal T}$. These are model inputs: this definition does not construct them or assume a general interacting continuum theory exists.

A **defect insertion** in $\mathcal T$ is data $(j,\lambda)$ where $j:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M^\circ$ is a smooth embedding of a manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary whose image is closed in the interior $M^\circ=M\setminus\partial M$, and $\lambda$ is the complete model-specified field, operator, or boundary-condition data supported on $j(\Sigma)$, including any orientation, coorientation, framing, or label-transport rule the model requires. Its codimension is $d-\dim\Sigma$. It is an allowed entry of $\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}$ only when the model defines $C_{\mathcal T}(b;D_{j,\lambda};O_1,\ldots,O_n)$ for each stated admissible combined background and boundary datum $b$ and list of other insertions.

A **defect network** is data $D=(K,\{S_s,j_s,\lambda_s\}_{s\in S},\{J_t\}_{t\in J})$ in which $K\subset M^\circ$ is closed, $S$ is finite, $K=\bigsqcup_{s\in S}S_s$ is a smooth stratification, and each $j_s:\Sigma_s\to S_s$ is a diffeomorphism from a smooth manifold without boundary onto its locally closed embedded stratum. The closure of each stratum is a union of strata, with the frontier condition that if $S_t$ meets the closure of $S_s$ and $S_t\ne S_s$, then $S_t$ lies in that closure and has smaller dimension; the incidence relation records exactly these pairs. Each stratum carries its complete model-specified field, operator, boundary, orientation, coorientation, framing, and other label data $\lambda_s$ as required; $J\subseteq S$ is the set of junction strata, and each $S_t$ with $t\in J$ carries a model-specified junction operator $J_t$ with an ordering of all incident labels. The model must declare which such networks and other insertions form admissible inputs of $\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}$ and define their correlators. A one-stratum network with no junction stratum is the preceding single defect, and a list of strata or a picture without its field and junction data is not a defect insertion.

An **isotopy** of a defect network is a smooth one-parameter family of its stratum embeddings $j_{s,t}:\Sigma_s\hookrightarrow M^\circ$, $t\in[0,1]$, compatible on stratum closures and incidence data, whose stratification and incidence relation are unchanged and which creates no additional intersections. The model-specified transport maps carry every stratum label $\lambda_s$, framing or orientation, and junction operator along the family; the combined background and boundary data remain fixed, and the network stays disjoint from every other insertion throughout the deformation. A single-stratum defect is the one-element special case. Fix a field $k$. In the ordinary categorical case, a **finite semisimple fusion category over $k$** is a finite semisimple tensor category in the sense of the earlier fusion-and-multifusion definition. Concretely, it is a locally small category (each Hom collection is a set) whose Hom spaces are $k$-vector spaces and whose composition maps are $k$-bilinear. A monomorphism $u:Y\to X$ is a morphism for which precomposition $\operatorname{Hom}(Z,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Z,X)$ is injective for every object $Z$; a subobject of $X$ is an isomorphism class of monomorphisms into $X$. An epimorphism is defined by the dual cancellation condition. The category is abelian: it has finite biproducts, kernels, and cokernels, every monomorphism is a kernel, and every epimorphism is a cokernel. Each Hom space is finite-dimensional, and every object has finite length, meaning a finite composition series with simple quotients. A simple object is nonzero with only the zero subobject and itself as subobjects; every object is a finite direct sum of simple objects, and only finitely many simple isomorphism classes occur. It has a $k$-bilinear tensor bifunctor, a tensor unit $\mathbf 1$ with $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf 1)\cong k$, and a natural associator $\alpha_{X,Y,Z}:(X\otimes Y)\otimes Z\to X\otimes(Y\otimes Z)$ and left and right unitors satisfying the pentagon and triangle axioms.

For an object $X$, a left dual $X^L$ consists of morphisms $\operatorname{ev}_L:X^L\otimes X\to\mathbf 1$ and $\operatorname{coev}_L:\mathbf 1\to X\otimes X^L$ for which
$$(\operatorname{id}_X\otimes\operatorname{ev}_L)\circ\alpha_{X,X^L,X}\circ(\operatorname{coev}_L\otimes\operatorname{id}_X)=\operatorname{id}_X, \qquad (\operatorname{ev}_L\otimes\operatorname{id}_{X^L})\circ\alpha^{-1}_{X^L,X,X^L}\circ(\operatorname{id}_{X^L}\otimes\operatorname{coev}_L)=\operatorname{id}_{X^L}.$$
A right dual $X^R$ consists of $\operatorname{ev}_R:X\otimes X^R\to\mathbf 1$ and $\operatorname{coev}_R:\mathbf 1\to X^R\otimes X$ for which
$$(\operatorname{ev}_R\otimes\operatorname{id}_X)\circ\alpha^{-1}_{X,X^R,X}\circ(\operatorname{id}_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_R)=\operatorname{id}_X, \qquad (\operatorname{id}_{X^R}\otimes\operatorname{ev}_R)\circ\alpha_{X^R,X,X^R}\circ(\operatorname{coev}_R\otimes\operatorname{id}_{X^R})=\operatorname{id}_{X^R}.$$
The unitors are suppressed in these four composites. Rigidity means that each object has both kinds of dual.

For the ordinary fusion-category clauses below, write $\mathcal C$ for this category.

Choose representatives $i\in I$ of the finitely many simple-object isomorphism classes, with $0\in I$ representing $\mathbf 1$. For each $i,j,\ell\in I$, the **fusion multiplicity** $N_{ij}^{\ell}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ is the number of copies of $\ell$ in a semisimple decomposition of $i\otimes j$, so $i\otimes j\cong\bigoplus_{\ell\in I}N_{ij}^{\ell}\ell$. The associated fusion space is $V_{ij}^{\ell}:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(i\otimes j,\ell)$. For $D_\ell:=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\ell)$, simplicity makes $D_\ell$ a finite-dimensional division $k$-algebra and $V_{ij}^{\ell}$ a left $D_\ell$-module by postcomposition; its rank as a left $D_\ell$-module is $N_{ij}^{\ell}$. When $D_\ell=k$ (in particular for absolutely simple objects), $\dim_k V_{ij}^{\ell}=N_{ij}^{\ell}$.

For simple $i,j,k,\ell$, the associator induces an isomorphism between the two fusion-channel spaces
$$\bigoplus_{m\in I} V_{mk}^{\ell}\otimes_{D_m}V_{ij}^{m} \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ } \bigoplus_{n\in I} V_{in}^{\ell}\otimes_{D_n}V_{jk}^{n}.$$
Here $V_{mk}^{\ell}$ is a right $D_m$-module by $g\cdot d=g\circ(d\otimes\operatorname{id}_k)$, $V_{ij}^{m}$ is a left $D_m$-module by $d\cdot f=d\circ f$, $V_{in}^{\ell}$ is a right $D_n$-module by $f\cdot d=f\circ(\operatorname{id}_i\otimes d)$, and $V_{jk}^{n}$ is a left $D_n$-module by postcomposition. The isomorphism is defined by the semisimple decomposition identifications with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}((i\otimes j)\otimes k,\ell)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(i\otimes(j\otimes k),\ell)$, and the middle map sends $h$ to $h\circ\alpha^{-1}_{i,j,k}$. Thus its domain and codomain are the stated fusion-channel spaces, not unspecified multiplicity symbols. In chosen decompositions and bases these are the associator matrices; their coherence is the pentagon. The fusion datum includes the actual associator, unitors, and both duality structures, not just the integers $N_{ij}^{\ell}$; the unitors satisfy the triangle and the dual maps satisfy the four displayed snake identities.

A **tensor-invertible object** $D$ is an object for which some object $E$ satisfies $D\otimes E\cong\mathbf 1$ and $E\otimes D\cong\mathbf 1$. An object with no such two-sided inverse is **non-invertible**. Simplicity and tensor-invertibility are separate properties: an object can be simple and non-invertible, or a direct sum of invertible simple objects and non-invertible as a whole.

For the **finite semisimple fusion 2-category** convention, assume that $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero. A strict $k$-linear 2-category $\mathcal C$ has objects $A,B,\ldots$, a $k$-linear category $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(A,B)$ for each ordered pair, 1-morphisms as its objects, and 2-morphisms as its morphisms; horizontal composition is $k$-bilinear and strictly associative and unital, and satisfies interchange. A $k$-linear category is one whose morphism spaces are $k$-vector spaces and whose composition is $k$-bilinear. A finite semisimple $k$-linear category is an abelian $k$-linear category with finite-dimensional Hom spaces, finitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects, and every object a finite direct sum of simple objects; in each such category a simple object is nonzero with no nonzero proper subobject, using the ordinary categorical subobject convention above.

A functor between categories is **fully faithful** when it induces a bijection on morphism sets for each pair of objects. For 1-morphisms $p:A\to B$ and $q:B\to A$, an adjunction $p\dashv q$ consists of 2-morphisms (unit) $\eta:\operatorname{id}_A\Rightarrow q\circ p$ and (counit) $\epsilon:p\circ q\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_B$ satisfying $(\epsilon\star p)\cdot(p\star\eta)=\operatorname{id}_p$ and $(q\star\epsilon)\cdot(\eta\star q)=\operatorname{id}_q$, where $\star$ denotes whiskering by 1-morphisms and $\cdot$ denotes vertical composition of 2-morphisms. A 1-morphism $f:A\to B$ is **adjointable** when there are 1-morphisms $l,r:B\to A$ with $l\dashv f\dashv r$, with each adjunction carrying the unit, counit, and triangle identities just specified.

A zero object $0$ is an object for which each Hom category $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,0)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(0,X)$ is equivalent to the zero category, the category with one object and one morphism. A zero 1-morphism is a zero object in its Hom category. A 1-morphism $f:A\to B$ is **fully faithful** when for every object $X$, postcomposition with $f$ gives a fully faithful functor $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,A)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,B)$. A **subobject** of $B$ is an equivalence class of fully faithful 1-morphisms $f:A\to B$, where $f:A\to B$ and $g:A'\to B$ represent the same class exactly when there is an equivalence $u:A\to A'$ and an invertible 2-morphism $g\circ u\Rightarrow f$. A zero subobject is represented by a fully faithful 1-morphism whose domain is equivalent to a zero object. A 1-morphism $f:A\to B$ is an equivalence if there is a 1-morphism $g:B\to A$ and invertible 2-morphisms $g\circ f\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$ and $f\circ g\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_B$; two objects are equivalent when there is such an equivalence between them. A nonzero object (one not equivalent to a zero object) is **simple** when all its subobjects are represented by either a zero-domain 1-morphism or an equivalence.

An additive category is a category with a zero object and finite biproducts. A 2-category is **additive** when each Hom category is additive in this sense, it has a zero object, and finite direct sums of objects exist. For $A_1,A_2$, a direct sum $A_1\oplus A_2$ has inclusions $\iota_i:A_i\to A_1\oplus A_2$ and projections $\rho_i:A_1\oplus A_2\to A_i$ with $\rho_i\iota_i\cong\operatorname{id}_{A_i}$, $\rho_i\iota_j$ a zero 1-morphism for $i\ne j$, and $\operatorname{id}_{A_1\oplus A_2}\cong\iota_1\rho_1\oplus\iota_2\rho_2$ in its endomorphism category.

A **monad** on $B$ is a 1-morphism $E:B\to B$ with unit $\eta:\operatorname{id}_B\Rightarrow E$ and multiplication $m:E\circ E\Rightarrow E$ satisfying
$$
m\cdot(\eta\star E)=\operatorname{id}_E=m\cdot(E\star\eta),\qquad m\cdot(m\star E)=m\cdot(E\star m).
$$
It is **separable** when there is an $E$-bimodule 2-morphism $c:E\Rightarrow E\circ E$ such that
$$
c\cdot m=(m\star E)\cdot(E\star c)=(E\star m)\cdot(c\star E),\qquad m\cdot c=\operatorname{id}_E.
$$
The first equation says that $c$ respects the left and right $E$-actions, and the second says that it is a section of multiplication. An isomorphism of monads $\tau:E\Rightarrow F$ is an invertible 2-morphism respecting the units and multiplications: $\tau\cdot\eta_E=\eta_F$ and $\tau\cdot m_E=m_F\cdot(F\star\tau)\cdot(\tau\star E)$.

A **separable splitting** of $E:B\to B$ consists of an object $A$, an adjunction $\rho\dashv\iota$ with $\rho:B\to A$, $\iota:A\to B$, unit $\theta:\operatorname{id}_B\Rightarrow\iota\circ\rho$, and counit $\epsilon:\rho\circ\iota\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$, a 2-morphism section $s:\operatorname{id}_A\Rightarrow\rho\circ\iota$ with $\epsilon\cdot s=\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{id}_A}$, and an isomorphism of monads $E\cong\iota\circ\rho$, where $\iota\circ\rho$ has unit $\theta$ and multiplication $\iota\star\epsilon\star\rho$. A 2-category is **finite semisimple** when its Hom categories are finite semisimple, every 1-morphism is adjointable, it is additive, every separable monad has a separable splitting, and it has finitely many equivalence classes of simple objects.

Use the following semistrict monoidal 2-category convention (a Gray monoid). It adds a unit object $I$, strict $k$-linear 2-functors $L_A=A\otimes-$ and $R_A=-\otimes A$ for every object $A$, and for every pair of 1-morphisms $f:A\to A'$ and $g:B\to B'$ an invertible interchanger
$$\phi_{f,g}:(f\otimes B')\circ(A\otimes g)\Rightarrow(A'\otimes g)\circ(f\otimes B).$$
Write $A\otimes B=L_A(B)=R_B(A)$. The tensor is strictly unital and associative: $L_I=R_I=\operatorname{id}$, $L_A L_B=L_{A\otimes B}$, $R_B R_A=R_{A\otimes B}$, and $L_A R_B=R_B L_A$. The interchanger is the identity when either 1-morphism is an identity, is natural in both 2-morphisms, is compatible with composition in each 1-morphism variable, and is compatible with tensoring by an object in either variable. These are coherence axioms on the data, not consequences of a fusion table.

A left dual $A^L$ has evaluation $e_L:A^L\otimes A\to I$ and coevaluation $i_L:I\to A\otimes A^L$, with invertible 2-morphisms exhibiting $(A\otimes e_L)\circ(i_L\otimes A)\cong\operatorname{id}_A$ and $(e_L\otimes A^L)\circ(A^L\otimes i_L)\cong\operatorname{id}_{A^L}$. A **fusion 2-category** in this convention is a finite semisimple monoidal 2-category in which every object has left and right duals and the monoidal unit is simple.

Neither finite semisimplicity nor either categorical definition asserts unitarity: a dagger structure, positivity, and any unitary coherence are additional hypotheses and data. Define Pauli operators by $Z_j|\mathbf h\rangle=(-1)^{h_j}|\mathbf h\rangle$ and $X_j|\mathbf h\rangle=|\mathbf h+\mathbf e_j\rangle$. Adopt the finite quantum Ising model with Hamiltonian

$$
H_L=-J\sum_{j=1}^{L}(Z_jZ_{j+1}+X_j),\qquad J>0,
$$

where $Z_{L+1}=Z_1$, $J$ has units of energy, and $\hbar=1$. Euclidean propagation through a time interval $s\ge0$ is the exact finite matrix $e^{-sH_L}$, with $s$ in inverse-energy units. Correlators are matrix elements between arbitrary boundary vectors of finite ordered lists of observable matrices and these propagation factors.

Let $\widehat{\mathcal H}_L=\ell^2(\mathbb Z_2^L)$ have basis $|\widehat h_{1/2},\ldots,\widehat h_{L-1/2}\rangle$, with dual Pauli operators $\widehat Z$ and $\widehat X$ defined by the same formulas on half-integer sites. Define the original-to-dual Kramers–Wannier map $K_L:\mathcal H_L\to\widehat{\mathcal H}_L$ by

$$
\langle\widehat{\mathbf h}|K_L|\mathbf h\rangle=2^{-L/2}(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^{L}\widehat h_{j-1/2}(h_{j-1}+h_j)}.
$$

The reverse-oriented map is $K_L^\dagger:\widehat{\mathcal H}_L\to\mathcal H_L$. To give a single endodefect with the fusion convention below, use the explicit reflection identification $R_L:\widehat{\mathcal H}_L\to\mathcal H_L$ sending $|\widehat{\mathbf h}\rangle$ to $|\mathbf r\rangle$ with $r_j=\widehat h_{1/2-j}$ (all indices are periodic), and set $D_L=R_LK_L$. This is an isometry of the two spin bases and identifies the dual Hamiltonian with $H_L$. The matrix of $D_L$ is real symmetric: its exponent is $\sum_j r_{1-j}(h_{j-1}+h_j)$, whose coefficient matrix is symmetric in $\mathbf r$ and $\mathbf h$. Thus $D_L^2=K_L^\dagger K_L$. The original-to-dual map and its reverse also have the typed fusion $K_L^\dagger K_L=I+P_L$ and $K_LK_L^\dagger=I+\widehat P_L$. A repeated fixed half-site identification is not used for this square; it would retain a spatial translation. A defect line is a wrapping insertion of $D_L$ on a Euclidean time slice. Its allowed position changes are slides within gaps between fixed observable insertions. In this finite lattice model, topologicality means invariance under the declared local line slides; re-association of junction channels is a separate linear recoupling identity; no smooth continuum isotopy claim is made. A finite defect network has labels $\mathbf 1,\psi,\sigma$, represented on the chain by $I,P_L,D_L$, where $P_L=\prod_jX_j$. Its fusion spaces are one-dimensional precisely for

$$
\mathbf 1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf 1=a,\qquad \psi\otimes\psi=\mathbf 1,\qquad \psi\otimes\sigma=\sigma\otimes\psi=\sigma,\qquad \sigma\otimes\sigma=\mathbf 1\oplus\psi,
$$

and zero otherwise. Choose a basis vector in each allowed one-dimensional fusion space and define the associator in those bases as follows. Write $\epsilon(\mathbf 1)=0$ and $\epsilon(\psi)=1$; then

$$
[F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma}]_{ab}=2^{-1/2}(-1)^{\epsilon(a)\epsilon(b)},\qquad a,b\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi\},
$$

$$
[F^{\psi\sigma\psi}_{\sigma}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,\qquad [F^{\sigma\psi\sigma}_{\psi}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,
$$

and every other allowed associator coefficient is $1$. In the abstract channel category, the unit maps $\mathbf 1\otimes a\to a$ and $a\otimes\mathbf 1\to a$ have coefficient $1$. Each simple label is self-dual; its left and right evaluation and coevaluation maps have coefficient $\lambda_a$ in the unit channel, where $\lambda_{\mathbf 1}=\lambda_\psi=1$ and $\lambda_\sigma=2^{1/4}$, with zero coefficient in the $\psi$ channel for $\sigma\otimes\sigma$. These are categorical maps, distinct from the lattice triangle normalizations below.

For local lattice tensors, heights $h,h',\widetilde h$ range over $\mathbb Z_2$, with addition modulo $2$; height $0$ denotes the label $\mathbf 1$, height $1$ denotes $\psi$, and a vertex marked $\sigma$ denotes an empty site. Set $Q_{hh'}=\delta_{h',h+1}$. The two nontrivial height placements of a trivalent junction of two $\sigma$ lines and one $\psi$ line have the following weights: when the vertex between the two $\sigma$ lines has ordinary height $h$ and the other vertices are empty, the weight is $T_{\sigma\sigma\psi}(h)$; when that vertex is empty and the other two have ordinary heights $h,h'$, the weight is $T_{\sigma\psi\sigma}(h,h')$. Explicitly,

$$
T_{\sigma\sigma\psi}(h)=2^{-1/4}(-1)^h,\qquad T_{\sigma\psi\sigma}(h,h')=Q_{hh'}.
$$

The identity-defect termination tensors have the following four orientations: the first two represent the two local orientations of the $\sigma\otimes\sigma\to\mathbf 1$ unit channel, and the last two represent the two local orientations of the $\psi\otimes\psi\to\mathbf 1$ unit channel. In each case the dashed third edge has label $\mathbf 1$ and the two sloping defect edges have the indicated common label:

- For defect label $\sigma$, when the upper vertex has height $h$ and the two lower vertices are empty sites, the tensor is $2^{-1/4}$.
- For defect label $\sigma$, when the upper vertex is empty and the lower vertices have heights $h,h'$, the tensor is $\delta_{hh'}$.
- For defect label $\psi$, when all three site vertices are empty, the tensor is $2^{-1/4}$.
- For defect label $\psi$, when the upper vertex has dual height $\widetilde h$ and the lower vertices have heights $h,h'$, the tensor is $Q_{h\widetilde h}\delta_{hh'}$.

In the last orientation, $\widetilde h$ is the upper dual-basis height and $h,h'$ are the lower ordinary heights, all in $\mathbb Z_2$. The mixed index $Q_{h\widetilde h}$ uses the same $h$ as $\delta_{hh'}$; there is no second independent dual height. Reversed orientations use adjoint tensors; every fusion-forbidden label or height assignment has weight zero, and all components outside the stated domains are zero. The other allowed channels use their unit basis maps of coefficient $1$. These local triangles and the abstract channel maps above are the adopted junction data of this finite network model, not consequences of the fusion multiplicities alone.

The complete admissible input domain is declared as follows. Each input is a finite decorated lattice tensor network with boundary vectors or boundary tensors, arbitrary finite ordinary insertion matrices, propagation tensors $e^{-sH_L}$ (or their dual versions), and any finite number of the wrapping defects and local trivalent junction tensors above, with their oriented site orderings. Local height edges have index set $\{0,1\}$, empty-site edges have the singleton label $\sigma$, and row edges have index set $\mathbb Z_2^L$. Matching edges are contracted only when their index sets and model sides agree; reversal uses the stated adjoint tensor. Boundary vectors and all uncontracted indices are part of the combined boundary data. The correlator is the unnormalized complex number

$$
C(\Gamma;b;O_1,\ldots,O_n)=\sum_{\text{internal admissible indices}}\left(\prod_v d_v\right)\left(\prod_{t\in\Gamma}\mathcal T_t(\text{incident indices})\right),\qquad d_v=\begin{cases}1,&\text{ordinary spin site},\\\sqrt2,&\text{empty site}.\end{cases}

The product over $v$ runs over local patch sites whose factors are not already absorbed into a row tensor; row matrices have their displayed normalization. Every site weight is included once; if a site is split among patches, its positive factors are split with product $d_v$. Unit defect quadrilaterals carry $2^{-1/4}\delta_{a\alpha}\delta_{b\beta}$, and a duality quadrilateral carries $2^{-1/2}(-1)^{ab}$ at its two ordinary corners; forbidden assignments vanish. Junction recouplings compare the two local contractions with the same external height indices, including site factors; equality or a specified linear combination must hold before the rest of the graph is contracted.
